b7143338e322.title: folio-assistant-sci
b7143338e322.content: Scientific source material used by folios that formalise mathematics, and the methodologies for formalising it in Lean that this layer adopts from that material.

fc6997ca7ca0.title: What this layer holds
fc6997ca7ca0.content: . | The paper content adapter (content-adapters/, adapters/paper/): how a paper folio’s blocks become LaTeX, PDF and HTML, and how the suggest editor checks paper math. | Skills (skills/): authoring mathematics in Markdown and LaTeX, Lean formalisation and proof review, the proof, rendering and compute audits, and the integration watchers that run them on every change. | Tools (tools/): one node per command a skill or process calls, such as lean-build, lean-cache, latex-preflight, paper-latex-build and tex-snippet-validate, each with its inputs and outputs. | Library and methodologies (library/, methodologies/): the papers this layer reads, and the Lean formalisation methods adopted from three of them. | .

17ef79a2665b.title: Processes
17ef79a2665b.content: Three BPMN processes in processes/content/ say who does what: . | Authoring a paper. The author (a person) plans the paper. The authoring agent seeds the work plan, scaffolds the folio repository and authors blocks. The Lean toolchain role formalises claims in Lean, and the build pipeline validates the folio and renders the PDF and HTML. | Publish a folio’s Lean render. The doc-gen4 HTML of a folio’s Lean package, staged under its site with the harness navbar and rail. | Atomic mass drift check. Whether AtomicMass.lean still matches its data table. | . Each process has a generated checklist beside it for an agent that walks the steps by hand.

d8efd7040ad5.title: Tutorial — writing a paper with folio-assistant
d8efd7040ad5.content: TR… . On this page . | The end-to-end workflow | Before you start | Step 1 — Plan the paper | Step 2 — Scaffold the repository . | Required .gitignore baseline | . | Step 3 — Author the content | Step 4 — Formalize in Lean | Step 5 — Validate | Step 6 — Render | Step 7 — Review & feedback | Step 8 — Publish | What you end up with | Where to go deeper | . This page is generated from docs/source/guides-writing-a-paper/ — each section below links to its own source. ✎ Edit QA… TR… . This tutorial walks through authoring a rigorous scientific paper with an LLM driving folio-assistant: the agent plans the paper, drafts blocks, formalizes theorems in Lean 4, renders LaTeX, and publishes — while you steer. It uses a small running example, “A note on the harmonic series”, to illustrate the workflow.

cb55e02ac386.title: The end-to-end workflow
cb55e02ac386.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… KG… . BPMN 2.0 source · full-size SVG . Every step is something the LLM does for you by calling folio-assistant’s MCP tools — you converse in natural language and approve the work. Approve is literal: steps 3–5 are a loop, and the assistant’s edit is a proposal until you have seen the validation findings and accepted it. The publication workflow models that gate, and the review and release that follow, as BPMN swimlane diagrams.

cbaf4e806d82.title: Before you start
cbaf4e806d82.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | Install folio-assistant and run bun run cat check-deps. For papers you want bun, latexmk/texlive, and Lean (elan). | Connect your LLM harness (Claude Code, Antigravity, …) so the agent has the MCP tools. | Create an (empty) content repository for your paper and add a <name>.config.json with "contentType": "paper". | .

24e92417bbc3.title: Step 1 — Plan the paper
24e92417bbc3.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Start by asking the agent to load the planning skill and propose a structure. Behind the scenes it calls skill_fetch content-plan. You: I want to write a short paper, “A note on the harmonic series”. It should define the partial sums, state and prove that the series diverges, and include one worked example. Plan it out. Assistant: (loads content-plan) Here’s a proposed plan: . | prose — Introduction & motivation | definition def:harmonic-partial-sum — the partial sum $H_n$ | theorem thm:harmonic-diverges — $H_n \to \infty$ | proof prf:harmonic-diverges — Oresme’s grouping argument | example ex:H4 — compute $H_4$ | . The definition and theorem will get Lean counterparts. Shall I scaffold the repo and create these blocks as drafts? . You: Yes, go ahead. This is also where you’d open work-plan items so the plan survives across sessions: . beans create "Draft harmonic-series paper: blocks + Lean" beans <id> --status in-progress .

5a0cb12a4dfb.title: Step 2 — Scaffold the repository
5a0cb12a4dfb.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The agent creates the block files and a main.tex, then confirms with content_list. Assistant: (creates blocks, calls content_list) Scaffolded 5 blocks under content/harmonic-series/. Current artifacts: . content/harmonic-series/ ├── 00-intro.prose.md ├── 10-def-partial-sum.definition.md ├── 20-thm-diverges.theorem.md ├── 21-prf-diverges.proof.md └── 30-ex-h4.example.md . Each block carries typed front-matter validated against the content-object model. A definition block, for example: . --- kind: definition id: def:harmonic-partial-sum title: Harmonic partial sum lean: HarmonicSeries.partialSum --- For $n \ge 1$, the *$n$-th harmonic partial sum* is $$ H_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{1}{k}. $$ . Required .gitignore baseline . ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Every new folio repository starts with these entries. Agent sandboxes accumulate scratch directories as untracked state, and a single git add -A then commits all of it under a message describing something else. # Agent scratch state — transient tooling state, never repository content. # Leading slash = root-level only. Keep it (see the warning below). /.agents/ /amalgamated_done/ /amalgamated_input/ /_deprecated/ /scratch/ .claude/worktrees/ # Python bytecode __pycache__/ *.py[cod] . Keep the leading slashes. A gitignore pattern with no internal slash matches at every directory depth, not just the root: unanchored, _deprecated/ would also catch a nested archive such as computations/_deprecated/, and scratch/ every content/**/scratch/. An ignore rule never untracks a file, but any new file under such a path is skipped by git add with no error and no output. If your folio keeps a nested archive or scratch area under one of these names, the anchored form keeps it committable. Two deliberate exclusions: . | beans/ stays tracked. It is the durable, cross-session work plan; a sibling agent has to be able to read it. Bean duplication is prevented by the create-guard of the todo-manager skill, not by ignoring the directory. | Any directory your folio documents as a real pipeline stays tracked — in qou, uploads/ is the document-intake stage and belongs in git. Check your own AGENTS.md §Project structure before adding a path to this list: if it is documented there, it is content, not scratch. | .

49ba744dd16f.title: Step 3 — Author the content
49ba744dd16f.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Ask the agent to draft prose and statements; review and refine conversationally. You: Draft the introduction and the divergence theorem statement. Assistant: (loads content-author, edits the blocks) Done. The theorem reads: “The sequence $(H_n)$ is unbounded; equivalently $\sum 1/k$ diverges.” I kept the statement Lean-friendly so it maps cleanly to Filter.Tendsto. A mock of the chat-driven authoring session: .

622c9040b41b.title: Step 4 — Formalize in Lean
622c9040b41b.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Now the agent sets up Lean and formalizes the definition and theorem, calling lean_setup, lean_build, and lean_check. You: Formalize the definition and theorem in Lean and make it build. Assistant: (loads lean-formalization; calls lean_setup) Toolchain ready (Lean 4.16.0). I added: . namespace HarmonicSeries def partialSum (n : ℕ) : ℝ := ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, 1 / (k + 1 : ℝ) theorem diverges : ¬ ∃ B, ∀ n, partialSum n ≤ B := by sorry -- Ref: [oresme] grouping argument . (calls lean_build) Build is green with 1 sorry remaining. (calls lean_status) Proof coverage: 1/2 blocks fully proved. You: Discharge the sorry using the grouping bound. Assistant: (edits, lean_build) ✅ Build green, 0 sorries. proof-verification reports the axiom set is clean (no sorryAx). sequenceDiagram participant You participant LLM as Assistant participant MCP as folio-assistant You->>LLM: Formalize + make it build LLM->>MCP: lean_setup MCP-->>LLM: toolchain ready LLM->>MCP: lean_build MCP-->>LLM: green, 1 sorry LLM->>MCP: lean_check / lean_status MCP-->>LLM: coverage 1/2 You->>LLM: discharge the sorry LLM->>MCP: lean_build MCP-->>LLM: green, 0 sorries .

dbe5d986c098.title: Step 5 — Validate
dbe5d986c098.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Validation checks every block against its schema and the project’s constraint rules (label prefixes, required Lean links, citation resolution, …). You: Validate the whole paper. Assistant: (calls content_validate) All 5 blocks valid. Constraints: def: block has its required Lean link ✓, theorem has a proof block ✓, example references a defined symbol ✓.

86518370c64f.title: Step 6 — Render
86518370c64f.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . The agent renders a PDF (and/or HTML) with the paper adapter. You: Render the PDF and show me a preview. Assistant: (calls paper_render_pdf, then paper_preview) Rendered harmonic-series.pdf (3 pages). Preview below. You can set rendering preferences (engine, scope, math renderer) via the paper_preferences tool: . You: Use lualatex and render only the theorem section next time. Assistant: (calls paper_preferences action=set latex_engine=lualatex render_scope=section) Saved.

ba4449d4c2bc.title: Step 7 — Review & feedback
ba4449d4c2bc.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Reviewer feedback is captured in the feedback store and routed back into the authoring loop (content-review / content-feedback). You: A reviewer says the example should also show $H_8$. Log it and address it. Assistant: (records feedback, edits ex:H4 → adds $H_8$, re-validates, re-renders) Done; feedback item resolved.

3e9795f01f5d.title: Step 8 — Publish
3e9795f01f5d.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . Finally, publish the rendered artifacts. In CI this is the publish workflow; locally the agent runs content_build and the render tools, then commits. You: Publish it. Assistant: (loads content-publish, content_build, commits + pushes) Published. PDF, HTML, and the Lean blueprint are built; the work-plan item is marked resolved. beans <id> --status resolved .

9e9e82cc3916.title: What you end up with
9e9e82cc3916.content: ✎ Edit QA… TR… . | A paper as a tree of typed, validated blocks | A Lean 4 formalization with zero sorrys and a clean axiom audit | PDF + HTML renders and an interactive blueprint | A reproducible CI pipeline (validate → build → render → publish) | .
